1523.subject: Physics
1523.text: Assertion : Generally the path of a projectile from the earth is parabolic but it is elliptical for projectiles going to a very great height. Reason : Up to ordinary height the projectile moves under a uniform gravitational force, but for great heights, projectile moves under a variable force.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1523.sol: Upto ordinary heights the change in the distance of a projectile from the centre of the earth is negligible compared to the radius of the earth. Hence projectile moves under a nearly uniform gravitational force and its path is parabolic. But for projectiles going to great heights, the gravitational force decreases in inverse poroportion to the square of the distance of the projectile from the centre of the earth. Under such a variable force the path of projectile is elliptical.

71335.subject: Biology
71335.text: The natural auxin produced by the placental tissue of the unfertilized ovary and responsible for enlargement of ovary into fruit is ---------------.
71335.sol: Auxins are a class of plant hormones that play a crucial role in various aspects of plant growth and development. Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) is the principal natural auxin found in plants. It is produced by the placental tissue of the unfertilized ovary and is responsible for the enlargement of the ovary into a fruit, a process known as parthenocarpy. Against the DPD gradient and with the expenditure of ATP (energy).
Against the DPD gradient and without the expenditure of ATP (energy).
Along the DPD gradient and without the expenditure of ATP (energy).
71548.sol: Active absorption of water by roots can be of two types: osmotic and non-osmotic. In non-osmotic active absorption, water is absorbed against the concentration gradient or DPD (Diffusion Pressure Deficit) gradient. Since the movement of water occurs against the natural gradient (i.e., from a region of higher DPD to a region of lower DPD), it requires the direct expenditure of metabolic energy in the form of ATP. Therefore, active absorption of water by roots is against the DPD gradient and with the expenditure of A

71690.subject: Chemistry
71690.text: Which of the following acid has the highest acid strength? (A) Acetic acid (B) fluoroacetic acid (C) 4-Nitrobenzoic acid (D) 4-Methyl Benzoic acid is
71690.sol: Acid strength is directly proportional to the stability of the conjugate base, which increases with the presence of electron-withdrawing groups (-I, -R effects). In fluoroacetic acid ( F-CH₂-COOH ), the highly electronegative fluorine atom exerts a strong -I effect from the adjacent -carbon, highly stabilizing the conjugate base. Its pK_a is approximately 2.59 . In 4-nitrobenzoic acid, the -NO₂ group exerts both -I and -R effects, but it is located farther away on the benzene ring. Its pK_a is approximately 3.41 .

72085.text: At resonance, the LC parallel resonant circuit
72085.sol: For a parallel LC circuit, the admittance is given by Y = 1 j L + j C = j ( C - 1 L ) . At resonance, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance, which means C = 1 L . 73808.sol: Sclerenchyma consists of long, narrow cells with thick and lignified cell walls having a few or numerous pits. They are usually dead and without protoplasts. Parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues. Xylem parenchyma is the only living component of xylem. Answer: Sclerenchyma

Water has a high boiling point
Water has a high heat of fusion

74277.sol: Water ( H ₂ O ) is a polar molecule due to uneven distribution of electron density. Water has a partial negative charge near the oxygen atom due the unshared pairs of electrons, and partial positive charges near the hydrogen atoms.

Cholera is a disease of muscles due to consumption of alcohol

74366.sol: Cholera is an infectious disease that causes severe watery diarrhea, which can lead to dehydration and even death if untreated. It is caused by eating food or drinking water contaminated with a bacterium called Vibrio cholerae.

79772.subject: Botany

79772.sol: In mitochondria, the inner membrane space is filled with a matrix which contains dense granules along with ribosomes and mitochondrial DNA. The mitochondrial DNA is circular in nature. There number varies from 2-6. Besides DNA, a mitochondrion has RNA and its ribosomes also. Thus, a complete protein synthesizing machinery is present in mitochondria, which suggests the semi-autonomous nature of mitochondria. Dictyosome, lysosome and peroxisome do not have their own DNA.

79861.subject: Botany
79861.sol: Kinetochore of chromosomes facilitates the attachment of spindle fibre (chromosomal fibre) and the poles. A chromosome consists of two identical halves, the chromatids which are held together at on point called the centromere. 80203.text: Which of the following statements regarding mitochondrial membrane is not correct ?
options: the outer membrane resembles a sieve
the outer membrane is permeable to all kinds of molecules
the enzymes of the electron transfer chain are embedded in the outer membrane
the inner membrane is highly convoluted forming a series of infoldings
80203.sol: In mitochondria, the outer membrane is semi permeable, and thus resembles a sieve permeable to all molecules of 10,000 Daltons. The inner membrane is selectively permeable and highly convoluted, forming a series of infoldings known as cristae. The enzymes of the electron transport chain are found in the inner membrane, while the outer membrane contains enzymes involved in mitochondrial lipid synthesis. Related Theory The inner membrane surrounds a central fluid-filled space called inner chamber or mitochondrial mat

Axial P - C l bonds are longer than equatorial P - C l bonds
P C l 5 molecule is non-reactive
80860.sol: (i) Three equatorial P - C l bonds make an angle of 120 ° with each other is correct. (ii) Two axial P - C l bonds make an angle of 180 ° with each other. (iii) Axial P - C l bonds are longer than equatorial because according to Bent’s rule the hybrid orbitals that contain more p - character or less s - character are placed on axial position and have more bond length. (iv) P C l 5 molecule is reactive (W) is the incorrect answer.

84830.sol: In the lac operon the z - gene codes for -galactosidase which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of lactose into its monomeric units, galactose and glucose. 84841.subject: Zoology
84841.text: In the lac operon, the z gene codes for :
84841.sol: In the lac operon, the structural genes are z, y, and a. The y gene codes for permease, which increases permeability of the cell to beta-galactosides. The a gene codes for a transacetylase. The i gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon. Answer: beta-galactosidase

114909.text: For a first-order reaction, the plot of [R] against time ( t in seconds) yields a straight line with a slope of -3.01 10⁻³ s ⁻¹ . The half-life of the reaction is:
114909.sol: For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate equation is: k = 2.303 t [R]₀ [R] Rearranging this equation gives: [R] = - k 2.303 t + [R]₀ Comparing this with the equation of a straight line y = mx + c , the slope ( m ) of the plot of [R] versus t is - k 2.303 . Given slope = -3.01 10⁻³ s ⁻¹ - k 2.303 = -3.01 10⁻³ k = 2.303 3.01 10⁻³ = 6.93 10⁻³ s ⁻¹ The half-life ( t_ 1/2 ) for a first-order reaction is: t_ 1/2 = 0.693 k = 0.693 6.93 10⁻³ = 100 s Answer: 100 s

127054.sol: Catalytic converters have platinumpalladium and rhodium metals as catalyst. It converts more harmful carbon monoxide and unburnt hydrocarbons into less harmful carbon dioxide and water.

127147.subject: Botany
127147.text: What is India's share of the global species diversity?
127147.sol: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent. That is what makes our country one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world. Nearly 45,000 species of plants and twice as many of animals have been recorded from India. How many living species are actually there waiting to be discovered and named? If we accept May’s global estimates, only 22 per cent of the total species have been recorded so far. 127462.subject: Botany
127462.text: The region of Biosphere Reserve which is legally protected and where no human activity is allowed is known as :
127462.sol: Biosphere reserve is protected area with multipurpose activities. It has three zones (i) Core zone - without any human interference (ii) Buffer zone - with limited human activity (iii) Transition zone - human settlement, grazing cultivation etc. are allowed.

127638.subject: Botany
127638.text: If we completely remove decomposers from an ecosystem, the ecosystem functioning will be adversely affected because:
options: Herbivores will not receive solar energy
Rate of decomposition of other components will be very high
127638.sol: This is because the recycling of minerals is done by detritivores only if they are removed the mineral movement will be blocked. Detritivores (e.g., earthworm) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called fragmentation. By the process of leaching, water soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.

127870.sol: In all ecosystem the maximum amount of energy is found in trophic level 1-r t ₁ (i.e. the producers) which keeps on decreasing along the higher trophic level.

127883.subject: Zoology

options: Organization into organs and organ systems
127883.sol: The basic tissues as you have learnt in earlier classes, organise to form organs which in turn associate to form organ systems in the multicellular organisms. Such an organisation is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells constituting an organism. Each organ in our body is made of one or more type of tissues . The colour of the dorsal side of the body is olive green with regular spots
Eyes are bulged out and are covered by a nictitating membrane
128010.sol: Body of a frog is divisible into its head and trunk. A neck and tail are absent. Above the mouth, a pair of nostrils is present. Eyes are bulged and covered by a nictitating membrane that protects them while in water. On either side of the eyes a membranous tympanum (ear) receives sound signals.

130747.subject: Zoology
130747.text: Which of the following options correctly identifies the contraceptive method, its category, and its corresponding mechanism of action?
options: Cervical caps - Barrier method - Inhibits ovulation
Coitus interruptus - Natural method - Prevents spermatogenesis
Copper T - Barrier method - Suppresses sperm motility
Tubectomy - Surgical method - Blocks gamete transport
130747.sol: Tubectomy is a surgical method (sterilisation) in females where a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up. This blocks gamete transport and thereby prevents conception. Cervical caps are barrier methods but they do not inhibit ovulation; they prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix. Coitus interruptus is a natural method that prevents insemination by withdrawal of the penis just before ejaculation, but it does not halt spermatogenesis. Copper T suppresses sperm motility

131248.subject: Zoology

131248.sol: Statement I is correct as cyclic menstruation is an indicator of the normal reproductive phase, which begins at menarche (the first menstruation at puberty) and ends at menopause (cessation of cycles around 50 years of age). They worked with viruses that infect bacteria called bacteriophages. The bacteriophage attaches to the bacteria and its genetic material then enters the bacterial cell. The bacterial cell treats the viral genetic material as if it was its own and subsequently manufactures more virus particles. These sequences show a high degree of polymorphism and form the basis of DNA fingerprinting. Since DNA from every tissue (such as blood, hair-follicle, skin, bone, saliva, sperm etc.)from an individual shows the same degree of polymorphism, they become a very useful identification tool in forensic applications. Further, as the polymorphisms are inheritable from parents to children, DNA fingerprinting is the bas

132027.subject: Zoology
132027.text: Which branch of biology deals with the inheritance and variation of characters?
132027.sol: These and several related questions are dealt with, scientifically, in a branch of biology known as Genetics. This subject deals with the inheritance, as well as the variation of characters from parents to offspring. Inheritance is the process by which characters are passed on from parent to progeny; it is the basis of heredity. Variation is the degree by which progeny differ from their parents

133657.sol: IgE is an anti-allergic antibody. It plays a pivotal role in response to allergens such as anaphylactic drugs, bee stings, etc. They are synthesised by plasma cells. It is found in only mammals.

133982.sol: Cotton is a dicotyledonous crop. The best biofertiliser for cotton is Bacillus subtilis and Azotobacter chroococcum. These are free living nitrogen fixing bacteria and enhance the fertility of soil.

A specific DNA sequence responsible for preserving genetic information
A specific DNA sequence responsible for multiplying alien DNA

Insertion of a foreign DNA fragment at this site causes insertional inactivation of the tetracycline resistance gene, making the recombinant plasmids sensitive to tetracycline. The ampicillin resistance gene remains intact. Therefore, the recombinant E. coli colonies will be resistant to ampicillin but sensitive to tetracycline. 6a13e465688ac6d0667aacf9.text: A train travels the first one-third of the total distance between two stations at a constant speed of 30 km/h . It covers the remaining two-thirds of the distance at a constant speed of 90 km/h . The average speed of the train for the entire journey is:
6a13e465688ac6d0667aacf9.sol: Let the total distance be d . Time taken to cover the first one-third of the distance is t₁ = d/3 30 = d 90 . Average speed is given by the total distance divided by the total time: v_ avg = d t = d d/54 = 54 km/h . Answer: 54 km/h

6a16f3297cfacf7984f86738.subject: Biology
6a16f3297cfacf7984f86738.text: Which of the following features is NOT associated with the members of phylum Arthropoda?
options: Body covered by a chitinous exoskeleton
6a16f3297cfacf7984f86738.sol: Phylum Arthropoda is characterized by the presence of jointed appendages, a chitinous exoskeleton, and an open circulatory system. In an open circulatory system, blood is pumped out of the heart and the cells and tissues are directly bathed in it. Excretion in many arthropods takes place through Malpighian tubules. Therefore, a closed type of circulatory system is not a feature of arthropods. Answer: Closed type of circulatory system

Reason (R): At electrical synapses, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, allowing electrical current to flow directly from one neuron into

Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fbe.sol: At electrical synapses, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity. This allows electrical current to flow directly from one neuron into the other across these synapses. Because of this direct flow of current, the transmission of an impulse across electrical synapses is very similar to impulse conduction along a single axon. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct

95054.subject: Physics
95054.text: Sound waves in the air are always longitudinal because
options: Of the inherent characteristics of sound waves in air
Air does not have a modulus of rigidity
Air is a mixture of several gases
Density of air is very small
95054.sol: In the transmission of sound through air, there is no actual movement of air from the sound producing body to our ear. The air layers only vibrate back and forth, and transfer the sound energy from one layer to the next layer till it reaches our ear. This back and forth motion causes the compression and rarefaction in a sound wave. This motion is along the direction of propagation of sound and hence, the sound waves are longitudinal. 97975.text: Girdle experiment involves the removal of ring wood of tissue outside the vascular cambium from the tree trunk. This leads to death of plant because

97975.sol: A simple experiment, called girdling, was used to identify the tissues through which food is transported. On the trunk of a tree, a ring of bark up to a depth of the phloem layer can be carefully removed. This simple experiment shows that phloem is the tissue responsible for translocation of food and that transport takes place in one direction, i.e., towards the roots. 306411.subject: Physics
306411.text: Identify the pair among the following that represents units of the same physical quantity.
306411.sol: Kelvin is the SI unit of temperature. Newton is the SI unit of force. Joule is the SI unit of energy. Calorie is a unit of heat energy. Therefore, Joule and calorie both represent units of the same physical quantity, which is energy.
